Create a voxel object

Source: R/create_3d_objects.R
as_voxel.Rd

Wrap a multi-depth raster as a SpatVoxel: the validated 3D form used throughout the package, with one layer per standard depth. Each layer's depth is stored in terra::depth(). Given a SpatProxy, as_voxel() reads one time step of it into memory instead. Reading a SpatProxy is experimental, like the class itself (see SpatProxy), and may change without notice while the core object is built.

Usage

as_voxel(
  x,
  depths = NULL,
  varname = "value",
  depth_bounds = NULL,
  time = NULL,
  time_match = c("nearest", "exact"),
  max_time_diff = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A SpatProxy, a SpatRaster, a list of SpatRasters (one per depth, combined with terra::rast(), which keeps their depths only when each has them set; otherwise pass depths), or an existing SpatVoxel. This is how gridded data enter the SpatVoxel model: describe a netCDF file with as_proxy() and pass the proxy here, which reads the time steps you choose with time. Crop the proxy first with terra::crop() to read only part of the grid. netCDF paths aren't accepted directly.

depths

Optional numeric vector, one depth per layer, in metres. When supplied, it sets the depths, and the layers are named {varname}_depth={value}, replacing any existing names. Required if x has no depths in terra::depth(). Leave it out, and depth_bounds too, for a SpatProxy, which gives its own.

varname

Character. Variable name used in the layer names built from depths, or from a proxy's depths, where it defaults to the proxy's variable name; it is also stored in terra::varnames(), which renaming the layers keeps. Ignored otherwise.

depth_bounds

Optional two-column matrix or data frame: the top and bottom of the slab of water each layer stands for, in metres positive down, one row per layer of x in its current order (for example a netCDF file's depth bounds). A data frame with columns depth, lower and upper, such as depth_bounds() of another voxel, is matched to the layers by depth instead. Each slab must contain its depth and have a positive height, and slabs must not overlap. NULL (the default) keeps the edges an existing SpatVoxel carries, unless depths renames its layers; a voxel without edges uses the bounds argument of the functions it is passed to.

time

For a SpatProxy only: which time steps to read.

  • NULL (the default) reads the only step of a proxy that has one; a proxy with more needs time.

  • A step number reads that step.

  • One date or date-time (a Date, POSIXct, or text such as "2020-01-02" or "2020-01-02 06:00", read as extract_to_point() reads observation times) reads one step: the nearest, or an exact match, as set by time_match. A date is compared by UTC day, so it matches the step on that day; with several steps a day, give a date-time.

  • A window of two dates or date-times (start, end) reads every step inside it, as a list. The window includes both ends; with dates, it covers whole UTC days including the end day, as a polygon's interval does in as_vector3d(). A window with no step inside it is an error.

  • A SpatVector3D with one feature reads the steps for that feature, always as a list, so a loop over shapes gets one kind of result: a point's time picks one step as a date-time does (a list of one), and a polygon's time interval is a window. On a source with one time step, such as a World Ocean Atlas climatology, that step is read whatever time the feature has, or none, so dated observations can be read against a climatology. On a source with several steps a feature without a time is an error. Lines are an error; buffer_3d() turns them into polygons.

time_match

For a SpatProxy with one date or date-time in time. "nearest" (default) reads the closest step; when time is exactly halfway between two steps, the step on the same UTC day wins, and otherwise the earlier one. "exact" reads the step on the same UTC day (for a date) or at the same instant (for a date-time), and is an error when there is none. The same rule as in extract_to_point(). Not used for a window.

max_time_diff

For time_match = "nearest": the largest allowed gap, in days, between time and the step read. NULL (the default) sets no limit. A gap beyond it is an error. As in extract_to_point().

Value

A SpatVoxel whose layers are ordered shallow to deep. For a SpatProxy with a time window or a SpatVector3D in time, an unnamed list of such voxels in time order, one per step, each with its step's date in terra::time(), even when that is one step.

Details

A voxel read from a proxy carries the proxy's depth edges (see depth_bounds()): the file's depth bounds, or, for a file without them (such as Copernicus Marine), edges halfway between levels, from the surface to half a gap below the deepest level. Because the voxel has edges, the bounds argument of volume() and the other 3D functions doesn't apply to it, and each layer stands for the same slab of water whichever layers are selected. To use other edges, pass them with as_voxel(v, depth_bounds = ...). A single level without bounds has no edges, so bounds applies.

The depths come from depths when it is given, and otherwise from the raster's own terra::depth(), which terra also sets when it reads a netCDF file. A raster with neither is an error: layer names are labels, never read as depths.

Most terra operations (crop(), mask(), [[, arithmetic, c()) keep the class and the depths; a few, such as mean(), return a plain SpatRaster instead. Re-wrapping is cheap either way: given a valid SpatVoxel and no depths, as_voxel() returns it untouched.

Keeping the class doesn't re-run the class checks, so an operation that changes the layers can leave an object labelled SpatVoxel that isn't a valid one (for example v[[c(1, 1)]], two layers at the same depth). as_voxel() checks such an object as it would a plain raster: unsorted layers are sorted, and the rest is an error. A voxel whose depths terra dropped, for example in app(), needs depths again (see SpatVoxel).

Depths are positive metres increasing downward, matching the World Ocean Atlas convention. Negative depths are an error rather than being silently negated, since flipping the sign would change what the data mean.

Examples

r <- terra::rast(nrows = 2, ncols = 2, nlyrs = 3)
terra::values(r) <- runif(terra::ncell(r) * 3)

# set the depths from a vector; the layers get readable names
v <- as_voxel(r, depths = c(0, 100, 200), varname = "temp")
depths(v)
#> [1]   0 100 200
names(v)
#> [1] "temp_depth=0"   "temp_depth=100" "temp_depth=200"

# depths already in terra::depth() are used as they stand, and sorted if
# needed
terra::depth(r) <- c(200, 0, 100)
depths(as_voxel(r))
#> [1]   0 100 200

# layer names aren't read as depths: a raster without terra::depth() needs
# `depths`
named <- terra::rast(nrows = 2, ncols = 2, nlyrs = 2, vals = 1)
names(named) <- c("temp_depth=0", "temp_depth=50")
try(as_voxel(named))
#> Error : The raster has no depths in terra::depth(). Pass `depths` to as_voxel(), or set them with terra::depth(). Layer names aren't read as depths. terra drops the depths in some operations, such as app(); see ?`SpatVoxel-class`.

# carry each layer's slab of water, as a netCDF file's depth bounds give it
v <- as_voxel(r, depth_bounds = cbind(c(150, 0, 50), c(250, 50, 150)))
depth_bounds(v)
#>   depth lower upper
#> 1     0     0    50
#> 2   100    50   150
#> 3   200   150   250
